note: args.canvas makes the picture the call draws on, w x h, uint8 RGB: with only "flat", that colour everywhere; with "mul" and "add", pixel i (counted row by row from the top left) has the channels (mul[c] * i + add[c]) % 256, and if "rows" [ya, yb] is there too only rows ya to yb - 1 are woven like that and the rest is "flat". "out" is the picture after the call. draw_captions: caps is the list of (t0, t1, lines) with the times as float.hex() strings; a keyword that is absent was not passed (y0 100, cx 180, base CREAM, hi AMBER, alt SKYB, puff (236, 204, 150); puff null is puff=None); expect.noted is what the call appended to reelkit.ui.DRAWN: [x0, y0, x1, y1, kind, info]. Cases with source "kit.picture" hold the caption list and keywords kit.picture.render passes for the example episode, at the time of the frame named. impact_landings: expect.returns rows are [t_land, line, chars]. Python scalar maths (math.sin for the shake, ** 2 for the punch) is the C runtime of the reference PC's.
